sources.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.caveat: FAO fills gaps for non-reporting countries using the trading partner's figures. Every row we publish carries FAO's own flag, so a reader can see whether a number was reported by that country or estimated for it.

sources.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.dataset: Food Balances: Supply Utilization Accounts, 2010 onwards (bulk download)
sources.plain_name: Where each country's wheat comes from and goes
sources.caveat: Opening stocks are FAO estimates for most countries. They are the best open figures available, and they are not a count of what is in store.

sources.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.plain_name: What food costs in the shops, month by month
sources.caveat: Compiled by FAO from IMF and national statistics offices. Countries report at different speeds, so the newest month differs by country.

sources.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.dataset: Cost and Affordability of a Healthy Diet (bulk download)
sources.plain_name: How many people cannot afford a healthy diet
sources.caveat: Modelled from retail prices and income distributions, not from a survey of households. It shows what a healthy diet would cost against what people earn, which is not the same as asking people what they ate.

sources.dataset: Commodity Markets monthly price data (the "Pink Sheet")
sources.plain_name: World wheat, fertilizer and energy prices each month
sources.caveat: These are world reference prices. They are not the price any particular buyer paid, and they are not the price in any shop.

sources.plain_name: Foreign currency reserves, imports and population
sources.caveat: National figures. A country holding plenty of foreign currency does not mean its households can afford food.
